summary: Task 21.4 (Live pinned-host verification) is correctly and completely implemented. The v1.2 matrix is recorded in docs/implementation/21.4/live-verification.json as live-host-verifier status VERIFIED with all eight rows L1-L8 PASS, and the four items the acceptance criterion names are each covered by concrete, cross-consistent live evidence: the status panel/endpoint (L5), the MB/KB byte round-trip and the seven restart-required note texts (L3), Extra Large (L4), and the bounded log subject (L6). I independently verified the record rather than accepting the verifier's own verdict: the artifact identity it recorded matches docs/release/build-and-release.md and the actual artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip on disk (619,538 bytes; SHA-256 50580499...f90762; MD5 3100aae9...5271; 7 entries) byte-for-byte; no secret appears anywhere in the file (all credentials appear only as the placeholders '<admin>', '<admin-token>', '$RADARRKEY', '$SONARRKEY'); every structural claim the record makes about the product reconciles with the source (the 9-top-level-field / 28-leaf-path diagnostics shape is 7 scalars + 3 MatchingFailures + 18 RenderFailureCounts, and RenderFailureCounts.cs has exactly 18 public counters; the seven restartRequiredNote divs and the Small/Medium/Large/ExtraLarge option order match config.html; the recorded L2 configuration defaults match the OperationalLimits.cs source defaults; the D-format item-id fallback matches LogSubject.cs:49; the step-multiple rejection is genuinely page-side, confirmed against ADR-028 clause 1 and the byteLimitToBytes implementation at config.html:412, with OperationalLimits.Validate enforcing only the byte range). I also confirmed the L4 PASS is a genuine third-pass re-run on a fresh host prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.4b and not a reclassification of the earlier contaminated run: the third_pass block records its own prefix, window, and rows_not_re_run, the L4 row carries a distinct second narrative with a different item-id set and different baseline/ExtraLarge identities from the /tmp/arrtags-21.4 run, and the decisive new datum is that the movie item which was permanently OwnershipLost on the first prefix (9eee318f...) rendered normally at Extra Large on the clean prefix (2e6e6620... -> 18,029 bytes), which a reclassification could not produce. The scope is exactly the four permitted files plus the two new evidence files: no code, test, artifact, manifest, changelog, limitations-register, or release-state change. PLANS.md and state.json follow the single-writer rule, render-docs-state.cs --check is clean, and I confirmed by probe that scripts/check-docs.sh returns PASS once this reviewer report is present and listed. The F-21.4-4 bounds are honestly stated and correctly qualified rather than papered over, and each is an already-registered accepted limitation rather than a new gap. The worker's known_limitations are accurate and not hidden. No user decision is required.

Each of the four named items maps to a row with concrete observed values: status panel/endpoint -> L5 (anonymous GET /ArrTags/Status 401 fail-closed, administrator 200 with a 9-top-level/28-leaf fixed-shape snapshot, admin POST/DELETE 405, sibling /ArrTags/Stats 404, and a secret/path/item-id/payload scan returning 0 matches; the served page carries only the static-hidden empty diagnosticsPanel div); MB/KB round-trip and note text -> L3 (exact byte counts 1572864 / 204800 / 1048576 POSTed through the elevation-gated save path returned 204 and read back identically from both ArrTags.xml and the administrator GET, with the seven-field unit/step/precision/min/max mapping and all seven restart-required note texts confirmed on the served resource); Extra Large -> L4 (Renderer.Size=ExtraLarge accepted with 204, activated with no host restart, and the served bytes changed to the new persisted ActiveImageIdentity on 3 of 3 eligible items on the clean prefix); log subject -> L6 (bounded file-name subjects and the D-format item-id fallback, 0 ArrTags lines containing '/tmp/' or '/media/', 0 occurrences of either mock provider key in console.log, and the bounded render classification on the artwork-boundary line). All four are PASS.

findings.detail: The single most important thing to check was whether the L4 PASS was earned on a genuinely fresh host or was a reclassification of the earlier contaminated run. It is earned. The third_pass block records its own prefix (/tmp/arrtags-21.4b), its own window (2026-09-29T12:05:00Z/12:12:30Z), and an explicit rows_not_re_run list of the other seven rows. The L4 row carries a second, distinct narrative appended after the first-pass PARTIAL text, and it is evidentially distinguishable from the /tmp/arrtags-21.4 run: a different item-id set (3d37d379.../181b3d99.../2e6e6620... versus c282a364.../9eee318f.../6d88ce4e...), different Medium baseline identities, and a test movie that had never previously rendered at Extra Large. The decisive datum is that the movie item which the first pass drove into the unrecoverable OwnershipLost state (9eee318f..., which the record states cannot return to a publishable session in v1.2) rendered normally at Extra Large on the clean prefix (2e6e6620... -> 18,029 bytes / 6ce051bc...876c). A reclassification of the old run could not produce that observation, and the old prefix's blocked movie is explicitly recorded as left untouched and still OwnershipLost. I also confirmed the verifier did not weaken the trigger discipline to get there: the third pass used POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/<ArrTags task id> and explicitly issued no POST /Library/Refresh after the first publication, which is the exact discipline F-21.4-5 recommends recording. The contamination is attributed to the library refresh, not to Extra Large, and F-21.4-2 and F-21.4-5 remain open on their own substance.

findings.detail: I assessed the recorded structural bounds on their merits rather than accepting the verifier's framing. The pinned host is launched by scripts/provision-jellyfin-test-host.sh with --nowebclient, so the settings page's client-side JavaScript and the diagnostics panel's inline JavaScript genuinely cannot execute; the repository also has no JavaScript runtime. I confirmed the host procedure states this explicitly at docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md ('--nowebclient ... the settings-page JavaScript and the browser modal are not exercised by this live matrix'), so it is a pre-existing documented property of the pinned host, not a bound invented to excuse a gap. Each of the three bounded surfaces is already a registered, accepted v1.2 limitation rather than an unrecorded shortfall: the diagnostics panel is V12-F3-1 ('verified structurally, not executed', LOW, accepted), the restart-required modal is V12-G8-1 (LOW, accepted), and the off-step byte-limit surface is V12-G6-1 (LOW, accepted). Crucially, none of the four items the acceptance criterion names is thereby unverified: the criterion names the status panel/endpoint (L5 verifies the endpoint live, including anonymous 401 fail-closed, which is the security-relevant half) and the MB/KB round-trip and note text (L3 verifies the byte round-trip live through the real save path and the note texts on the served resource; the display-value conversion is the bounded part, and the criterion's 'round-trip' obligation is the byte round-trip, which is live). I independently confirmed the step-multiple claim is accurate rather than an excuse: ADR-028 clause 1 states the existing OperationalLimits.Validate 'enforces only the field's byte range, not step alignment' and assigns the explicit step check to the settings conversion path, config.html:412 implements exactly that (bytes % stepBytes !== 0 -> null), and OperationalLimits.Validate contains only AddRangeError range calls with no step logic. So the live observation that an off-step 1572865 is accepted and stored as bytes is the documented design, correctly reported as a bound and not as a defect. The Extra Large safe-area clamp/shorten-omit path is likewise bounded, and the criterion's 'Extra Large' item is about the size option being offered, accepted, applying at runtime without restart, and changing the served bytes, all of which are live-verified; the clamp is additionally covered by committed unit-level tests and goldens (BadgeLayoutTests, RendererBehaviorTruncationTests, RenderGoldenFixtures with ExtraLarge policies). I judge these acceptable, correctly qualified bounds for a live verification. One observation recorded as a noted non-defect: the F-21.4-4 wording and the L3 note both correctly preserve the 'PASS for its live-observable scope' qualifier rather than claiming a live round-trip of the display conversion, which is the honest framing.

findings.detail: I spot-checked the record's quantitative and structural claims against the source to confirm it reflects a real run rather than plausible-looking prose. The L5 claim of '9 top-level fields and 28 leaf paths' reconciles exactly: DiagnosticsSnapshot has 9 public properties, and 7 scalars plus 3 MatchingFailures plus 18 RenderFailureCounts properties equals 28, with RenderFailureCounts.cs containing exactly 18 public counters. The L3 claim of 'exactly 7 restartRequiredNote divs' and the L4 dropdown-order claim (Small, Medium, Large, Extra Large) both match config.html, which has 7 restartRequiredNote occurrences and the options in that order. The L2 recorded configuration defaults match the OperationalLimits.cs source defaults (QueueCapacity 512, ProviderResponseLimitBytes 8 MiB, WebhookMaxPayloadBytes 256 KiB, Source/DerivedArtifactLimitBytes 32 MiB, MaxImageDimensionPixels 8192, RenderCacheQuotaBytes 1 GiB, ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes 4 GiB, TerminalProvenanceRetentionDays 30, InventoryCacheMaxRecords 10000, InventoryCacheMaxBytes 32 MiB). The L6 D-format fallback matches LogSubject.cs:49. The L3 claim that an out-of-range POST is rejected without persisting is consistent with Plugin.cs:143-157, which validates before calling base.UpdateConfiguration so an invalid candidate is never written. The F-21.4-3 attribution of the [ERR] lines to a pre-existing host-internal CollectionFolderMetadataService condition is corroborated by the same condition recorded in docs/implementation/14.3/live-verification.json. The F-21.4-6 uninstall residue claim is consistent with the source contract the record cites (TryDrainForUninstall then TryDeleteStateRoot). These checks increase confidence that the record is a faithful account of a real run.
